column1: # tools/doom/core-refusals.tsv — the original's "not implemented" raises, and what reaches each.
# The original (examples/doom/lib/doom) is a partial DOOM: where it meets
# something it does not implement it raises LevelError and the program stops.
# The port transmits each such raise as core_fail(:capacity) at the same call,
# because CORE has no other failure (the owner's decision of 2026-09-17; its
# reason is written at each port site). This table names every such raise in
# the Game files -- tests/doom-core/refusals.rb refuses a raise with no row and a
# row with no raise -- and what stands behind the claim that the port stops
#   scenario:NAME   tests/doom-core/scenarios.rb's NAME, a `stops` scenario whose
#                   `stop_in` is the row's port definition: both stop at the
#   claim:TOKEN     no shipped content reaches it; the ledger row's claim, checked
#   full:NAME       Full refuses before calling the entry (Session#before_step!),
#                   shown by scenario NAME (`full_refuses`); the same scenario run
#                   with --no-full-guard shows the port's backstop refusal
#   setup           it raises while Full loads the level, before any entry runs;
#   unchecked:WHY   nothing in the suites stands behind it; WHY says what was
#                   measured once, by hand, and is a LIMIT, not a claim. THESE
#                   ROWS ARE THE SOFT PART OF THIS TABLE: no suite re-measures
#                   them, and a change to the library or the IWAD can make one
